svg.title: Fig. 99 — y = x^x, with the dotted branches for x < 0
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 99, page 104. Section: discontinuous.

g.data-text: For x > 0 the curve starts at the open point (0, 1) (x^x → 1 as x → 0+), falls to its lowest value (1/e)^(1/e) ≈ 0.69 at x = 1/e, and then climbs steeply.
For x < 0 the points are everywhere discontinuous: they exist only at rational x, with the value ±|x|^−|x|, and lie on the dotted curves; the lower dotted curve for x > 0 is −x^x.
